title: Knowledge check: One-Way Data Flow

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “One-Way Data Flow”?
options: Copy every prop into independent local state without a reason.
Use slots only for passing Boolean values.
Pass parent-owned data through props and emit an event when a child requests a change.
Mutate a prop in the child as the default update pattern.
questions.answer_key: Pass parent-owned data through props and emit an event when a child requests a change.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses One-Way Data Flow directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Parent-to-child communication”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Every component should keep a private copy of all props.
Props flow down from parent to child; children emit events to request parent-owned state changes.
Child components should mutate props freely.
Slots can only contain plain text.
questions.answer_key: Props flow down from parent to child; children emit events to request parent-owned state changes.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Parent-to-child communication”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “One-Way Data Flow” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
